title: BDGPork
ingredients: 2 Tablespoons fresh thyme or 2 teaspoons dried
pinch each of nutmeg and cinnamon
1/2 dried cranberries, available in most grocery stores either with produce or the nuts
directions: Mix marinade ingredients and let pork marinade overnight in the frig. Let set at room temperature 1 hour before grilling. Grill on hot grill for about 3 minutes per side and then cook on the fourth and final side till browned – it should be juicy and pink – 135-140. Let rest and slice on bias. Pour sauce over and serve.

In a large saucepan reduce port to 1 cup over high heat. Add whip cream, pepper and thyme. Reduce over medium heat until sauce thickens. Add 1/2 cup dried cranberries and simmer 2-3 minutes longer. Sauce can be made well in advance. This dish is a little pricey but is well worth the cost, the sauce is fabulous. Garlic mashed potatoes and gingered carrots and broccoli make good accompaniments. OR

Adjust oven rack to middle position; heat oven to 400 degrees. Sprinkle tenderloins evenly with salt and pepper; rub seasoning into meat. Heat oil in 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until smoking. Place tenderloins in skillet; cook until golden brown on all sides, about 5 minutes total. Transfer tenderloins to rimmed baking sheet and place in oven (reserve skillet if making pan sauce); roast until internal temperature registers 135 to 140 degrees, 10-15 minutes. Rest & slice.

Immediately after placing pork in oven, add 1 tablespoon butter to still-hot skillet; when melted, stir in 2 chopped shallots, 1 tsb brown sugar, and 2 Tbs water. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, until shallots are browned and caramelized, 7 to 10 minutes; set skillet aside off heat.

While pork is resting, set skillet over medium-low heat and add 3/4 cup vinegar; simmer, scraping up browned bits with wooden spoon, until mixture is slightly thickened, 5 to 7 minutes. Add rosemary and any accumulated pork juices; continue to simmer until syrupy and reduced to about 1/3 cup, about 2 minutes longer. Off heat, whisk in mustard and remaining 3 tablespoons butter, one piece at a time. Adjust salt and pepper.
Or, a deglazed sauce of marsala, butter, and sage (maybe a fried leaf).
Mix all ingredients except the tenderloin.
Smear the rub over the tenderloin. Roast covered 25 to 30 minutes or until 135 to 140 on a meat thermometer.
